text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Increase metformin to 1000 mg twice daily and set an individualized HbA1c goal below 7.5%; avoid insulin and sulfonylureas while autonomic neuropathy may blunt warning symptoms of hypoglycemia
  • Endocrinology consultation to confirm diabetic autonomic neuropathy as the cause of orthostatic hypotension, reconsider the earlier Shy-Drager label, and choose add-on glucose-lowering therapy
  • Treat neurogenic orthostatic hypotension: stand up in stages, raise the head of the bed, use waist-high compression, drink 2 liters of fluid a day, then midodrine with the last dose at least four hours before bed; check supine blood pressure at each visit
  • Check HbA1c every three months until at goal, a basic metabolic panel, UACR, and lipids each year, lipids 4 to 12 weeks after starting a statin, and vitamin B12 periodically on metformin
  • Examine the feet at every visit because of sensory loss; daily self-inspection and protective footwear
  • Coordinate glaucoma care with the eye clinic: add dorzolamide to latanoprost, check pressure at each visit, and repeat OCT and visual fields every six months; avoid timolol and brimonidine because of bradycardia, bronchospasm, and low blood pressure
  • Annual dilated eye examination for diabetic retinopathy; low-vision rehabilitation and home lighting review
  • Start atorvastatin 40 mg; give PCV20 and recombinant zoster vaccines

resource.title: Johnny Cash synthetic care plan
resource.description: Recognize that orthostatic lightheadedness, leg numbness, and falls in an older adult with long-standing type 2 diabetes fit diabetic autonomic and peripheral neuropathy rather than a prior label of Shy-Drager syndrome; set an individualized HbA1c goal, choose glucose-lowering drugs that avoid hypoglycemia, treat neurogenic orthostatic hypotension, and coordinate glaucoma care so that eye drops do not worsen blood pressure, using the CMID diabetes and glaucoma schedules.
